items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: before Martin and several other things happened... before Martin Luther King and President Johnson and other people saw things happening in our country

ctx.x: When you were traveling on the road with Erskine Hawkins or any of the other bands, what was the hardest part of that, being on the road?

Well being on the road at that particular time, when I left Erskine the Civil Rights Act, this was before Martin and several other things happened. But the Civil Rights Act had just become a reality in our country. There wasn’t some of the things, some of the violence hadn’t started to happen. But people had begun to think for themselves you know what I mean. It even started down south. And there were hotels that we couldn’t go in, there were restaurants that we couldn’t eat in. And things, what were called…
